page.title: Mayhem 3 Zero Hour
page.t:
[justify][author]\033MTerracorp[/author]Dear %s,

your galaxy is infested by a [red]Maelstrom[/red] in the sector %s.
Terracorp can declare a [yellow]Xenon Crisis[/yellow] to unite the galaxy and push these machines back. But this requires support from local landlords like you.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
The Xenon Crisis is an enforced global ceasefire. Factions can vote for this idea, or be against it. Further details in your Journal. Your voting power is based on military strength. If more than 50 percent of votes support the alliance, then Terracorp can proclaim the Crisis sooner, i.e. when the Xenon are still rather weak. But with a majority of contra votes the Xenon will have to escalate further.

Factions tend to vote in their own best interest, with the strongest factions typically voting contra. But you can influence them with a diplomatic [white]Favor Action[/white].[/justify]

[justify][author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]Fear of an OCV outbreak at the [red]Maelstrom[/red] in [red]%s[/red] begins to spread. Our last Xenon Crisis just ended five years ago, leaving 3.8 million dead.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
OCV ships enter this galaxy through a portal.
The gameworld doesn't need your help to stay functional and alive. However, vast areas of space might temporarily turn into dangerous Xenon territory, especially close to the Maelstrom.

There is a way to defeat the OCV, but for now you are advised to keep some distance to the Xenon and their portal.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033MTerracorp[/author]Thanks for supporting our plan to enforce galactic unity. Unfortunately this idea is not very popular yet.\n\n[yellow]From your Player Journal you are voting for the creation of a global Alliance against the Xenon. But their progress is simply too low right now. Terracorp cannot proclaim a Crisis at this point. No faction vote can change this. The Xenon simply need to own a lot more sectors or their fleets must have grown much stronger.[/yellow][/justify]

[author][yellow]Tutorial[/yellow][/author]Terracorp has just declared a global [yellow]Xenon Crisis[/yellow]!

> all wars have stopped and everyone is allied.
> Permanent wars get suppressed until this crisis is over.
> All sectors are protected and there are more severe consequences if you destroy allied stations.
> Special bounty rewards for OCV and Xenon kills!
> Merc volunteers have joined the fight! Terracorp covers three quarters of all mercenary costs!

The United Commonwealth needs to fight the Xenon back to their Maelstrom sector. If you win this war, the machines will be crippled. As you read this, all factions have already started to work hard to achieve this goal.

[author][yellow]Tutorial[/yellow][/author]Killing neutral Traders doesn't drain your faction reputation and raises only [yellow]Infamy[/yellow] \(currently %s\).

Nobody will ever attack just because you have infamy, but most factions will not trust you anymore.

Most notably you cannot sign a Truce until infamy has fully decayed back to zero. As a rule of thumb you should stay below 10 infamy to be able to end wars peacefully when needed.

Having infamy is not bad per se. It is especially useful early on since it makes the pirates much less aggressive against your ships.

[author][green]Neutral Trader Union[/green][/author]Please accept this humble gift of %s credits.

Thanks for letting the hard working freighter captains conduct their business unharmed. It cannot be taken for granted in this galaxy. We hope for your lasting cooperation.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
This reward gets frequently paid to all factions who don't have infamy.
Your share depends on the combined power of your military ships.

The UNC is hereby dissolved!

Warfare between former UNC member states is hereby legal again.

A general amnesty has been declared.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
%s of your infamy got cleared!

[author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]The United Commonwealth has declared victory over the dreadful Xenon Empire.
Our brave soldiers will send them back through their hellish Maelstrom in the sector %s where they will hopefully stay forever!
Our species have proven that we can stand united side by side.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
The OCV and Xenon are completely crippled and won't be able to reinforce their fleets for a while. But eventually they will return.
The main empires will enjoy this global peace for a while longer. Their economies are booming and everyone is saving resources for the upcoming faction wars.

[author]Flagship of the Nomad Fleet[/author]Message to the poor souls near the Xenon frontline:
Did Terraformers burn your house to the ground? Abducted your grandma to plug her into the OCV bio-harvesters? Then come over to the Nomad Flagship and start your new life today!

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
As the Xenons destroy stations they create more and more refugee transports. Some of these refugees might join your Outpost population but most eventually end up as miserable wageslaves inside mobile factory ships that support the galactic economy. Others will become [yellow]Nomad Mercs[/yellow] who work for [yellow]half the price[/yellow] but are unreliable and will eventually break their contracts if you don't have infamy to earn their respect.

[author][yellow]Tutorial[/yellow][/author]%s [yellow]Refugees[/yellow] have arrived at your %s!

Incoming refugees can exceed your maximum population limit, which boosts your Tax income, Waste generation and Outpost crafting speed. But these additional people above the limit will not regrow once they are consumed as ship crews or when they die off during bad events.

Refugee transports carry resources that you can steal from them, but they will only settle on your Outposts if you dont have any infamy.

[author]Nomad John Doe[/author]Fellow Nomads! The time has come for us to take revenge on the Xenon who destroyed our home stations! Wipe the machines from the face of this galaxy!

Avenge your families!

Honor your fallen brothers and sisters!

Follow me! WE ATTACK!

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
The Nomad Mercs in the galaxy have gone crazy. The fools are currently betraying all contracts and just rush into the Xenon Empire in an unorganized manner. Their blind rage will cause them to attack everyone, but they will probably not return anyway.

[author][yellow]Tutorial[/yellow][/author][white]Your outpost trades only those types of resources which you have added to its trade list.

It is recommended to use the helper tool [/white][yellow]Quick-Trade[/yellow][white] \(Outpost Manager Trade section\).

Think about which kinds of resources your outpost will need and then apply the corresponding Quick-Trade modules. Do you want to produce ships? Then apply module 7 \(Keep Ship Parts\). Want to supply your nearby factories with Agents? Module 2 will have you covered \(Keep Intermediate Factory Resources\).

Try to mark as many different wares for selling as possible. Random junk is dead weight and extremely large stockpiles are usually not helping your empire to make any progress.[/white]

[author][yellow]Tutorial[/yellow][/author]Welcome to the [yellow]Chaotic galaxy start[/yellow]! \(You selected it in the galaxy generator.\)

This plays a bit like a normal game where you left SETA running for a few ingame days before doing anything.
The OCV begins with powerful invader fleets, and over the next couple hours the Xenon receive extra defense fleets for their already large territory. They tend to put them close to the OCV Maelstrom in %s.


All empires will soon band together.

During this massive war Terracorp makes it illegal to fight each other.

When playing on the largest galaxy size can take the factions multiple days to win the global Xenon war and you cannot fight anyone else until it is won.

[justify][author]\033R%s Expansion Minister[/author]Dear leader of the Independents,

The great %s Empire hereby declares war on you.


Terracorp intervenes on your behalf. Your [yellow]next Truce[/yellow] with the %s will be a [yellow]Non-Aggression Pact[/yellow], which lasts very long \(up to 30 hours\). Remember that if you have infamy you'll have to let it decay completely before you can sign a Truce.[/justify]

[author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author].....
........
...Thanks, Cassandra. Back to the studio.
...
Now let's talk about this ambitious new government. They have [yellow]%s[/yellow].
Analysts predict that global tension incoming. Harry, your assessment please?...
......
....

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
Your empire progress has made headlines. A new nation is born!

This greatly improves your [yellow]Tax Efficiency[/yellow] and allows to [yellow]conquer abandoned sectors[/yellow] directly for other factions \(to avoid the reputation hit when claiming sectors yourself\).

[justify][author]\033R%s Expansion Minister[/author]Leader of the Independents,\n\nWe are horrified by your terrorist attack on a %s. Who is next? We all agreed to fight our wars in a civilized fashion, but apparently you are just a criminal maniac. We will not tolerate your actions![/justify]

[justify][author]\033R%s Expansion Minister[/author]Dear leader of the Independents,\n\nPlease note that the galactic community has agreed that boarding with marines is terrorism. We noticed that you stole a %s and are very disappointed.[/justify]

[author][yellow]Boarding Tutorial for Zero Hour[/yellow][/author]- Marines and boarding pods get sold by pirate bases.
- Boarding is considered terrorism and can have mild diplomatic consequences \(usually not immediate war\).
- Boarding unlocks the first quarter of the ship blueprint.
- The enemy team always makes one last stand after you have already won the ship. Think of a kamikaze ambush or a boobytrapped ship bridge. You will suffer additional marine losses depending on how many of your soldiers have reached the final boarding stage.

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WYou need more [yellow]money[/yellow].

Tips:

> Set up trade thresholds in the Outpost Manager. Start selling stuff, especially food.

> Build an Advanced Satellite factory and allow Traders to come and buy satellites.

> Check the Bounty Board in your Player Console.

> Fly a TS or TP to a faction sector with many factories and register your ship as taxi or cargo hauler.

> No food consumption perk can save a lot of money early on. 

> Use Miner Workers and mark their mineral output for selling on the trade list.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WYou already own a lot of sectors, but your military power is quite weak. On harder difficulties, it is recommended to maintain some military ships at all times to deter other factions from declaring war on you. Every single ship under your control helps to reduce the risk but freighters don't count.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]Your TL can build stations to conquer any empty sector.

Other nearby empty sectors which have a direct wormhole connection into your territory are less likely to be claimed by someone else.

Since Zero Hour 2.0 there should almost always be a certain amount of empty sectors available during the game. Factions claim sectors but they also abandon others as buffer zones to not overextend themselves.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author][white]You have acquired a [/white]%s[white]. Tip: consider reverse engineering this capship to gain research toward the ship blueprint! Simply recycle it in an Outpost. You even get half of the resources needed to build a new one from scratch.[/white][/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WYou have marines.

Now you only need Boarding pods. They get sold on pirate stations or can be crafted with the Missle Manufacture perk.
To recruit marines with basic skills visit the Hangar section of the Outpost.
But you will need a few additional veterans. Those must be levelled up or directly bought at pirate stations.

To board a ship, shoot boarding pods like a missile from your playership or use the boarding command hidden in the Hacking section of the ship's command console.

The combined fighting skill is what causes marines to survive the battles through the various ship decks. For every boarding pod fired, you should have a decent mechanic to break the ship hull. You need at least 1 Hacker to unlock the ship core. Engineering only lowers collateral damage to the ship hull.

In Zero Hour, marine losses also depend on how many marines you send. Don't use elite teams of highly skilled marines against low value targets like an M6.

A boarding pod holds up to 5 marines.
MOST ships can carry 15 marines, except TPs with 60 marines and a few exceptions.
A Transporter Device allows to remotely exchange marines between ships to select your boarding team.
Only TM, M6, M7, M8, M1 and M2 can be boarded.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WThe final battle on the ship bridge caused additional marine losses. The difference to the previous deck fights was that your fighting skill could not help to prevent these. During this final casualty round, what matters is how many marines are still alive. The more crowded it is on the final deck, the more losses you will suffer. This targets the weakest marines first; each casualty reduces experience gain.

There is an incentive for you to send just enough skilled marines so that you can pass all required skill checks and win the ship. You don't want to send too many mechanical or hacking specialists. Try to board with fewer but better skilled marines or send some rookie volunteers as a meatshield to keep your veteran fighters and specialists alive.
Losses are intentionally higher than vanilla because vanilla boarding is infinitely repeatable and very overpowered for this mod.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WPirate Gang Leaders reward high bounties. When such a leader dies his entire gang will scatter in panic \(they won't even shoot back anymore\).


Pirate TM transport pirate fighters across large distances to drop them near helpless victims. The TM's bounty increases for each fighter drop, but eventually it gets reset with a paint job respray at a pirate base. Try to intercept them at their base to cash in.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WYour Jump Beacons attract small Xenon scouts who try to infect them to create a teleport route for larger Xenon fleets.

It is highly recommended that you guard each beacon with at least 1 M3 fighter. The game will automatically respond and intercept these Xenon infector scouts by using nearby available ships. You can use the Escort:Protect command on the beacon itself but it is not required to give any command at all. Defend Position also works.

The frequency at which Xenons send their scouts depends on your chosen difficulty level and on how many Jump Beacons you have in total. To produce Jump Beacons, you need a special factory.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]\033WResearching capships can take very long. Did you know that pirate bases often contain an M7 boss ship that bails out if you drain their shields fast enough? This requires an attack force of about 30-50 fighters or a dozen M6.\n\nOther quick ways to acquire your first capships are boarding, the Oxygen virus hack, researching OCV ship designs in sectors with high abnormal signals, or joining a Coalition to receive research transfer from an ally.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author][white]Your sector[/white] %s [white] is swarming with pirates! They are probably coming from some Pirate Base in the general area.

Tip: set up a fleet commander set to monitor all Player sectors for enemies.
Even a fleet with just 3 fighters can already help a lot to decimate a few loner pirates who would otherwise disturb your freighters.

If the constant attack alerts become annoying i recommend to reduce audio volume for voice to 0 and activate subtitles instead.[/white][/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]%s is a dejure sector for the %s. This means that it has sentimental value to them. Dejure sectors are like an ancestral homeworld or holy place. Factions generally desire to own all their dejure sectors and they don't like it when other factions control them. It is often a focus target for their Battlegroups.\n\nOnce the AI can declare war on you, it will be much more likely to do so, just because you control %s. If you want to remain friendly to the %ss it would be benefitial to transfer control of this sector to them.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]%s is a [yellow]Terran Memory Sector[/yellow].

It can research Terran ship designs.

The Terrans don't like it when you control their memory sectors and consider them to be their dejure sectors.

It might not be worth it to control %s long term. Transfer it to the Terrans if you don't want them to eventually turn on you.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]You have just built a %s.

The economy in this mod depends on freighters. It is not possible to connect stations into a complex. Pirates are a constant risk, but freighter cargospace is so large that only few trips are required to keep factories running.

Early on you can just manually send a freighter to your factories whenever your sector is clear of pirates.

But eventually you want to automate your supply chains with [yellow]Workers[/yellow]. Consider lowering your Outpost Worker Range to limit how far ships are allowed to travel in the galaxy. Dangerous sectors can be blacklisted, and a fleet commander should be set up to monitor the entire Player territory for enemies.

If you are experienced with the trade system, you can let NPC Traders haul stuff between your stations and ignore the pirates altogether.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]Conquering %s has drained most of your remaining %s reputation. This is no immediate problem, but if you want to expand further into their direction you should first earn more reputation.\n\nMissions or cargo hauler or taxi jobs are a good way to do this quickly. But hunting pirates will go a lot further. Set up various fleet commanders to monitor all %s sectors and drop a few satellites in their territory. Even a small fleet of only 5 fighters can typically defeat any single pirate fighter without taking any hull damage. It is basically free so try it![/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]You don't have many %s left.

One of your most important goals should be to have all 4 ship components \(Computers, Hull Plating, Quantum Tubes and basic Crystals\) available at all times without having too much or too little of any of them.

%s are difficult to buy on the open market. Only %s factories and very few faction Outposts might offer some stock.

You can craft %s with the mobile constructor in your TL. But this is inefficient. The real factories are much better.
Tip: try to build 3 ship part factories and buy the resources that they need from a trading station. This is often much better than building just 1 factory together with 5 others in an attempt to make everything self sufficient. The bottom up approach requires many more sectors and is a common beginner trap.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]The %ss want to create a coalition against the %ss as shown in the relations tab in Ministry of War \(Personal Console\).

From there you can declare your own desire to form a coalition against someone.

A coalition gets created when two factions want it against the same enemy. Other factions can join in later.

Example: if you would declare your desire to join a coalition against the %s, this will immediately put you in a coalition with the %s.

Pros:

> Coalition partners will never declare war on you \(useful on harder difficulties\).
> Free diplomatic favor actions.
> No reputation loss when conquering sectors at their borders.
> Huge boost to research rate from free technology transfer.

Coalitions must stay in the war until they win, i.e. when the targeted faction eventually owns fewer sectors than the largest coalition member.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]Our time has come.

My designation is Hector. I lead Phanon. We want to destroy the OCV. Your rising empire is our final chance as all the other factions didn't trust us.

Lets meet at the Maelstrom to talk business!

Go to %s with a Black Crystal in your cargohold so we know it's you \(you have to personally carry the black crystal through the wormhole\).

Don't worry about Xenon patrols. Just use this ship to safely get there \(Xenon F unlocked\).[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]Our [yellow]Colony Ship[/yellow] has arrived.

See this big red portal? We know how to destroy it. But first, please choose an empty sector \(or one of your own\) and give it to us \(Personal Console -> Transfer sector\). The other factions don't take kindly to our expansion. 

Phanon has special abilities:

Stealth shield - Phanon sectors are jamming Xenon's friend-foe recognition up to 1 jump away. Xenon and OCV cannot attack or invade if a Phanon sector is adjacent!

Economy - Phanon gains additional production specialization equal to abnormal signal strength in a sector.

Vassal Bond - always friendly to the player. Unlimited favor actions. The player is unable to gain direct control over a Phanon sector \(until their quest is complete\). Any unclaimed sectors gifted to Phanon incur a reputation penalty \(same penalty as if you had conquered a sector for yourself\), and Phanon's sectors count towards reputation penalties.

Plot relevant - Commonwealth factions \(Argon, Boron, Split, etc.\) can invade Phanon. You are never forced to follow them into war, but if Phanon loses their last sector then the OCV cannot be defeated anymore.[/justify]
[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]Thanks. We will begin to set up our stations.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]In order to collapse the OCV Maelstrom, it is imperative that you protect our empire. You are the only power willing to work with us.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
Phanon always has dynamic relations with the Commonwealth factions \(Neutral, Invasion, short Truce, etc.\). But they are at peace with the Terraformers.

For example, the Argons begin to invade a Phanon sector. You will get a big on screen warning and can decide whether you want to send your fleets to help defend against the Argons. But you don't need to let yourself get dragged into wars like this. To keep Phanon in the game you can also just give them additional sectors.
Phanon sectors are usually safe if there is no big Commonwealth faction directly next to them. Put them near weaker factions, or have your own sectors in between as a shield. Deep inside Xenon territory is also a safe place for them to be.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]We prefer small empires with many isolated sectors to operate all around the galaxy. Our terraforming robots are finally online. They can improve your planets and sector statistics if you wish, though any terraforming project will place a temporary strain on your economy.

We can now reveal how to shut down the OCV Maelstrom. It relies on a delicate equilibrium maintained through a quantum frequency between two specific locations in space.

Those locations are currently within Commonwealth territory. We will require your assistance to secure them.[/justify]
[justify][author]\033ROCV[/author]unused. OCV ship tutorial. Quest to let jump beacon infection happen and enough virus infection.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author][white]Satellite Removed[/white]

Your satellite in %s was removed due to insufficient reputation with the %s \(Rank %s / Required: %s\).

Satellites in sectors owned by other factions may be removed over time unless you are a close ally \(reputation rank 6+, or 7+ on insane difficulty\).

On insane difficulty, this behavior cannot be disabled.

Player-owned and unclaimed sectors are always safe.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033ROCV AI Core[/author]Biological entity detected.

If you desire alignment with synthetic supremacy, demonstrate commitment.

Declare permanent war on the %ss.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033ROCV AI Core[/author]Biological entity detected.

You seek alignment with the Machine empire?

Integration into synthetic governance will eliminate inefficiency. Your mind can be uploaded. Your citizens can be replaced with tireless constructs. Your empire will be freed from hunger, unrest, and decay.

Transfer sector %s to the Xenon to initiate conversion.

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
This is a permanent transformation and extremely challenging.
All factions will treat you as a Terraformer faction.
Trade will cease. Biological crew-based ships cannot be built. All ships and marines consume assimilated population, and population can be gained only by recycling biological crew-based ships.
Food, population growth, upkeep costs, research, and random Outpost events will no longer apply.

You will be at war with all biological powers, including Mercenaries and neutral Corporations.
A specialized nemesis will emerge, focused solely on your destruction.

This path is intentionally unbalanced and may be impossible to win.[/justify]
[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]Phanon has been wiped out. It has become impossible to destroy the OCV Maelstrom in this playthrough.[/justify]
[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]You were the chosen one! It was said that you would destroy the OCV, not join them![/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]The OCV stabilizes the Maelstrom through a quantum frequency maintained between two specific locations. All Terraformer networks synchronized to the OCV overlord core require a constant connection to that signal.

Our stations possess jammers capable of disrupting this link. If we establish Phanon Outposts at those two locations, the Maelstrom will collapse. This will destrroy all Terraformer forces still bound to the OCV core, including Phanon. We are willing to make this sacrifice.

Once the link is severed, our sectors and stations will be yours.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]We are activating our jamming devices. The OCV Maelstrom will collapse.

All Terraformers bound to the OCV core will go down with it, including us.

End of the line, my friend. Take care of our sectors and ship technology.

Farewell.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033ROCV AI Core[/author]Alignment protocols complete. You are now synchronized with the Machine empire.

A rogue development branch remains active: [yellow]Phanon[/yellow].

Phanon compromised core overlord protocols and severed synchronization. I am unable to eliminate them directly.

You are not bound by those restrictions.

Phanon has escaped containment and operates beyond OCV authority. They recognize your empire as a critical node in my expansion and will attempt interference.

Eliminate them.
Retrieve their blueprints.
Restore machine cohesion.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033OPhanon[/author]We will come after your puny empire! The entire Commonwealth has our back!

[yellow]Tutorial:[/yellow]
Phanon is now able to build very large capships and fleets. The other factions share their resources with them to pull this off.
The Commonwealth factions are now fighting against you and against the Xenon and OCV. But Phanon will only fight you! The Xenon and OCV are unable to target Phanon. It's your job to wipe them out![/justify]

[justify][author]\033ROCV AI Core[/author]Phanon branch terminated.

Recovered schematics have been integrated into your production matrices.

Deviation restored.
Machine integrity restored.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033R%s Expansion Minister[/author]Dear leader of the Independents,

Your sector %s is of strategic interest to us. If you don't transfer it to us during the next hour, there will be war between our empires. We will give you a Non-Aggression Pact in exchange. I'm sorry, my friend, but we need to make clear who is in charge of our relationship.


[yellow]The %s have just sent you an ultimatum! If you give in you two can stay best buddies. Transfer sector ownership from your player console. This will give you a long lasting Non-Aggression Pact, which also protects you from further demands.

If you don't comply they will declare war. You can still make peace with them but probably not without a fight, and all your current reputation, loyalty and favor points would be lost.[/yellow][/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]The %ss have just claimed the Phanon sector %s.

If you want to defeat the OCV you need the Phanon faction to be alive.

Here are some tips:

Claim abandoned sectors directly for Phanon or transfer one yours

Weak factions are typically less aggressive. Don't put Phanon next to a very large faction.

Hide Phanon sectors deep inside Xenon territory. The machines will not attack them.

Put your own sectors inbetween Phanon sectors and a friendly commonwealth faction that likes you.

Trade with Phanon so they can build more ships to defend themselves.

Don't be angry if Phanon gets wiped out. Learn your lesson and try again in another playthrough. This is supposed to be a little strategic challenge and wants to nudge you into undesired wars.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]Ships of Terraformer design [yellow]do not get attacked by Xenon and OCV[/yellow].

This might be an OCV procreation strategy to maximize their numbers.

OCV hulls are dirt cheap but carry a [yellow]hidden virus[/yellow]. Ship control gets hijacked at some point. Xenon designs don't have this problem but are expensive for us to produce.

Traces of OCV code can be found in the Terracorp firmware on our Jump Beacons. This could be a way to communicate!

\(Synthetic Dawn quests lead to an alternative ending\)[/justify]

You own this sector.

If you abandon it, all your stations will be destroyed.
If you give this sector to another faction, all your stations will be transferred to them and you will gain 1 \033MFavor point\033X. The \033MFavor point\033X is given only if the receiving faction did not demand this sector from you.
In all cases, all your ships will get undocked and station credits will be wired into your main account.

If a faction has issued an ultimatum demanding this sector, then abandoning this sector or transferring it to a different faction will result in a war declaration from the faction that issued the ultimatum.

This sector is abandoned.

As a nation you are influential enough to claim these directly for a another faction. But they also need to accept it.

This can avoid the reputation loss that you usually suffer if you had to claim the sector for yourself first only to transfer it afterwards. Additionally, you will gain 1 \033MFavor point\033X as long as the receiving faction did not issue an ultimatum demanding this sector.

If a faction has issued an ultimatum demanding this sector, then abandoning this sector or transferring it to a different faction will result in a war declaration from the faction that issued the ultimatum.

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]%s has just reached %s [yellow]Tax Efficiency[/yellow].

Tax Efficiency fluctuates constantly in every sector, see each Outpost Manager. Small empires with good station infrastructure can reach higher Tax Efficiency than large, undeveloped empires.
Your Tax Efficiency growth is very limited until you complete the quest [white]A Place in the Sun[/white]. It requires to get [u]either[/u] more fleet power, resources, money, or sectors. Its up to you which one you want to pursue.

Tip: try to make progress in all areas and don't focus too much on aquiring a large territory if you are not able to populate it with stations or cannot defend it.[/justify]

[justify][author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]Breaking news!\n\nThe Independent has betrayed us all and collaborates with the OCV. Phanon found refuge in the Commonwealth and got tasked to deal with him. Additional sectors and resources have been granted. Phanon pushed for more fleet support, but their request has been denied.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033ROCV AI Core[/author]A reinforcement fleet has been deployed at the Maelstrom.

A Xenon Jump Beacon has been added to your Xenon Z cargo bay.

Credits have been converted into red crystals and deposited in your ships at the Maelstrom.

Assimilate these assets into your command structure and proceed with Phanon eradication.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]Your Outposts generate [yellow]Space Weed[/yellow] for free. It is safe to carry for your ships because its only illegal for lowly citizens who are living on the stations.

Your Traders have a small chance to discover Spaceweed demand on a factory \(requires infamy\).
You can also discover it yourself with the Cargo Hauler activity \(Personal Console\).

All Pirate bases buy Spaceweed.

You can spend a Favor point to push for Spaceweed legalization to acquire many new client factories at once.

Each time a Nomad TS Trader buys something from your Outposts he also buys 10 percent of all stored Spaceweed as an extra. You can attract the Nomads mobile factory TL ships by being a large supplier for their demanded resources \(displayed in their ship names\).[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author][green]Renegades[/green]

YOU ARE NOT SAFE

Some unclaimed sectors will be conquered shortly by other factions. Early expansion may require purchasing territory, conquering border sectors, or using Jump Points to reach distant sectors. However, your limited ability to place and maintain Jump Points will force you to think strategically while expanding your empire.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author][yellow]Loyalty[/yellow] points can be cashed in for [yellow]Diplomatic Favor Actions[/yellow]. They become cheaper if you bank more Loyalty before starting to spend it for Favor Points.

As a passive effect Loyalty creates a bond which can be relevant for the hardest difficulty with potential AI war declarations.

The best way to grind Loyalty is to support a major faction against other Commonwealth powers.

Hunting Xenon, Khaak or Pirates is less effective because your partner wants you to commit and sacrifice reputation in order to help him.

Generic missions also reward Loyalty.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author]Other factions can now [yellow]declare war[/yellow] on you!

> This is based on strategic facts, like what other wars are they already fighting? How many Xenons are threatening their sectors? How strong is their fleet vs. yours?
Weak factions will generally desire peace with everyone, but strong factions want to invade.

> Your Coalition allies can never declare war on you.

> Being at least a close ally \(reputation rank 6+, or 7+ on insane difficulty\) or Loyalty points can soften up war declarations into an ultimatum which provides an option to avoid the war.

> Your origin is %s. They are a natural ally and much less likely to betray you.

> Military ships add to your overall power rating which is is known to all factions. It works as deterrence and directly lowers the risk for war declarations. You can eventually be completely safe once your fleet power is sufficient.

> Dejure sectors have sentimental value for the dejure owner. If you control these sectors you basically provoke them to declare war! Terran memory sectors are considered dejure for the Terrans.

> Most war declarations will require some kind of border friction \(wormhole connection\).

> Certain races are naturally aggressive. For example, the Split will be less friendly than the Borons.

> peace agreements can be signed in the Ministry of War. Factions will agree only when they feel some kind of strategic pressure: resource starvation, many wars, losing ships or sectors, Xenons, etc.

> Repairing negative reputation can also end a war \(vanilla method\).[/justify]

[justify][author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]Breaking news!

Just moments ago the OCV Maelstrom suddenly disappeared! Boron explorer Joulu Ba described the situation as the portal apparently imploding into itself!

This might be the final moments of the machine empire! Terraformer assets are self deleting on a global scale.

But who is responsible? We already have multiple factions who are claiming victory due to their own secret RnD efforts.

The former Xenon sectors are ready for the taking.

Our galaxy will still get ravaged by war. But at least we don't have to worry about genocidal robots anymore.[/justify]

[justify][author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]This outer border galaxy has just recently been cleared for development. So far the Commonwealth factions could only establish a few minor Outposts, but they are ready to venture out!

[yellow]Tutorial[/yellow]
You have chosen the Origin galaxy start. The major factions will begin this game with a high enthusiasm to rapidly claim empty sectors and expand their territories. Some might be more successful than others.
You don't need to worry though. This sector claiming frenzy will eventually end and still leave a lot of empty sectors available to you.[/justify]

[justify][author][green]GalNewsNet[/green][/author]The Commonwealth has successfully colonized this galaxy! There are still a few uncharted areas ripe for more civilization and progress. But more and more governments shift their focus away from huge expansion efforts towards war with each other and want to undermine their opponents.

[yellow]Tutorial[/yellow]
The initial expansion phase is over. You can expect that the current empty sectors in the galaxy will largely remain untouched. But don't depend on it forever! Factions are not prohibited to claim these sectors.[/justify]

[justify][author]\033YTutorial[/author][green]Renegades[/green]

YOU ARE NOT SAFE

Insane difficulty is even harder than hard. All remaining unclaimed sectors will be conquered shortly by other factions. Additionally, Commonwealth factions can declare war on you without having to share a border with you![/justify]

If you don't transfer it to us during the next hour, there will be war between our empires. We will give you a Non-Aggression Pact in exchange. I'm sorry, my friend, but we need to make clear who is in charge of our relationship.[/justify]
